note: SIMULATED: outputs of apps/sim/src/sim.ts under the constants below; not measurements.

constant_sources.arrivalWindowMin: COMPETITION-PLAN.md §4 scale math (10k agents in 10 min)
constant_sources.zipfS: assumption; calibrated so ~22% of intents overlap a live intent at 1k agents (51% at 10k, 75% at 100k)
constant_sources.reviewLatency: assumption; reviewers modeled as unlimited (favors the baselines)
constant_sources.pConflictPerSharedFile: assumption; overlap is necessary, not sufficient, for a textual conflict
constant_sources.pFlake: assumption (per CI run); Google reports ~1.5% of test runs flaky (2016 testing blog)
constant_sources.pDefect: assumption (reaches CI with a real bug; 90% caught by the intent's own CI)
constant_sources.pInteraction: assumption (semantic conflict caught only on the combined SHA)
constant_sources.reviewMin: assumption (human minutes per small agent PR)
constant_sources.policy: DEFAULT_POLICY from intents-core.ts (lanes 50 per group x 8 parallel, speculation depth 3) + protected src/auth/**, migrations/**
constant_sources.trainsSpeculationDepth: 1: trains-only models the pre-speculation executor (one group in flight per repo)
constant_sources.dollarsPer1kOps: Artifacts pricing page ($0.15 / 1,000 ops; names create, push, pull, clone as examples); checked 2026-10-12
constant_sources.forgeFetchCache: design, not shipped: train caches item fork fetches across speculative rebuilds; replays fetch trunk once
constant_sources.git.forkPerIntent: Forge claim_intent forks once per intent (trains + forge modes); the baseline works on branches of the same repo
constant_sources.git.baselineFetchBeforePush: assumption: baseline agent runs pull --rebase before every push
constant_sources.git.fetchPerRebase: assumption: one trunk fetch per author rebase (conflict, interaction fix, escalation); a defect fix needs none
constant_sources.git.fetchPerReplayAttempt: train/replay code fetches trunk + the intent fork per attempt (2); 1 with forgeFetchCache
constant_sources.git.pushPerReplay: a successful replay pushes the re-derived head once
constant_sources.git.fetchPerRestack: assumption: a restack fetches the predecessor's current head once
constant_sources.git.queueFetchPerServe: assumption: the serial queue fetches trunk once per serve (bounces included)
constant_sources.git.queuePushPerServe: assumption: the queue pushes the updated branch / merge ref for CI
constant_sources.git.trainFetchPerGroup: apps/worker/src/train.ts buildGroup: fetchCovering(main) once per group (+1 for the speculative parent lane ref)
constant_sources.git.trainFetchPerItem: apps/worker/src/train.ts buildGroup: one fork fetch per item; LOWER BOUND (fetchCovering deepening retries ignored)
constant_sources.git.landPush: apps/worker/src/train.ts fastForwardMain: fetch lane ref 1, push main + push notes 2 (plus an ls-remote, reported apart)
constant_sources.git.probe: train-core bisect probes: fetch trunk 1 + each item 1, push the probe ref 1
constant_sources.git.pollIntervalsSec: assumption: projected agent poll intervals (git fetch every 30 / 60 / 300 s)
constant_sources.git.pollWindows: assumption: polls while working (lower bound) .. until landed or abandoned (upper bound); applied post-hoc, so fresher agents are NOT modelled as conflicting less
constant_sources.git.forgeSync: Forge agents sync from Feed events: 0 polls
constant_sources.git.lsRemote/token: ls-remote and token mints counted apart: Artifacts billing for them is undocumented

pull_note: pull_curve: SIMULATED git ops by kind per landed change; poll_projection is PROJECTED (git fetch every interval_s, applied post-hoc). Rows with variant forge-fetch-cache are a design, not shipped.
